column1: # *** NAVARRETE, LOGRONO - THE SEAM OPEN QUESTION 1 HAS BEEN POINTING AT, WORKED 12 OCTOBER 2026. ***
# Open question 1 has said since 11 October that Navarrete is "worth a day" - not because this
# archive believes Pablo Armando's father came from there, but because it is the only place it
# can name where LERENA y LERENA was a settled local usage, and it had never been looked at.
# *** THE SHORT ANSWER: THE REGISTERS ARE NOT FILMED, AND THE ONE PROMISING RECORD TURNED OUT TO
# BE GUADALAJARA. *** What came back instead is a defined job (the 1752 Catastro), a forename,
# a Spanish-born household in Buenos Aires five years before the escritura, and one more
# demonstration that a machine-doubled surname looks exactly like a real one.

column1: *** WHY NAVARRETE WAS WORTH A DAY ***
column2: open question 1 has named it since 11 October
column3: *** THE ONE PLACE THIS ARCHIVE CAN NAME WHERE THE DOUBLED SURNAME WAS SETTLED LOCAL USAGE ***
column4: On 14 November 1900, at the Spanish consulate in Buenos Aires, the brothers Prudencio Benito and Juan Jose *** LERENA y LERENA ***, naturales de Navarrete, provincia de Logrono, signed escritura 368 with their widowed mother *** Isabela LERENA y BASARAN. *** A Lerena had married a Lerena, in Spain, and the children carried it as a surname of record.
column5: *** The question was never whether the household is real - the escritura is read and transcribed. It was whether Navarrete's own registers would show the usage was ordinary there, and whether a Juan Carlos sits in them. ***

column1: *** THE CATALOGUE ANSWER, AND IT IS A HARD ONE ***
column2: FamilySearch catalogue, q.place = Navarrete, Logrono, Spain
column3: *** ONE SUBJECT. ONE ITEM. NO PARISH REGISTERS AT ALL. ***
column4: The place resolves (SEE: PART OF CASTILLA LA VIEJA, LOGRONO) and returns *** Census (1) *** and nothing else. No baptisms, no marriages, no burials, no diocesan series.
column5: *** SO THE NAVARRETE REGISTERS CANNOT BE READ FROM THIS DESK. *** They are not filmed and they are not in the full-text corpus - a full-text sweep for Lerena against Navarrete returns Llerena of Badajoz over and over and no Navarrete volume of any kind. *** This is a null about FamilySearch's holdings, not about the family, and it is the reason this seam now needs a person rather than a session. ***

column1: *** WHAT IS FILMED, AND IT IS WORTH HAVING ***
column2: Catastro del Marques de la Ensenada, Navarrete, Logrono, 1752 - Archivo Historico Provincial de Logrono, filmed 2007
column4: Vol. 481 Respuestas generales y Raiz de seglares | 482 Raiz de seglares | 483 *** Raiz y Personal de seglares *** | 484 Raiz de eclesiasticos | 485 *** Memoriales de seglares. *** Also in the online collection Spain, Catastro de Ensenada 1749-1756.
column5: *** A HOUSEHOLD-BY-HOUSEHOLD SURVEY OF THE WHOLE TOWN, taken in 1752. *** It will not name a Juan Carlos born in the 1840s, but it will answer the prior question underneath him: *** was LERENA a Navarrete surname at all before the 19th century, and was it already being doubled? *** Vols 483 and 485 are the personal ones. No waypoint established - film numbers only, and they have not been opened.

column1: *** THE 26 RECORDS THE INDEX CALLS NAVARRETE ***
column2: record index, surname Lerena exact, q.anyPlace = Navarrete, Logrono, Spain
column3: *** 26 - AND THE PLACE FIELD DOES NOT HOLD ***
column4: Controlled first: the same query at Reykjavik and at Osaka returns 0, so with m.queryRequireDefault=on the place parameter genuinely FILTERS. Spain holds 375 Lerena records, Logrono 27, Navarrete 26.
column5: *** THE FILTER WORKS AND THE DATA UNDER IT DOES NOT. *** The richest of the 26 - a marriage naming a mother *** Wenceslaa Maria LERENA LERENA *** - was opened at the plate and is *** San Gil de esta ciudad de GUADALAJARA, 21 December 1863 ***, two hundred kilometres from Navarrete. *** A place filter can only be as good as the place field, and here the field is wrong on the one record that mattered. ***

column1: *** AND THE COMPOUND WAS A MACHINE DOUBLING AFTER ALL ***
column2: the same marriage act, read at the plate
column3: *** THE ACT WRITES LERENA ONCE. THE INDEX WROTE IT TWICE. ***
column4: For an hour this looked like the second documented LERENA y LERENA in Spain, independent of the Buenos Aires brothers - which would have made the Navarrete usage look regional rather than one household's.
column5: *** IT IS NOT. *** Margin and body both read *** Wenceslaa Maria Lerena, natural de esta ciudad, e hija de Andres, ya difunto, y de Joaquina Lozano. *** One surname, her father's; her mother is a LOZANO. *** So the archive's own compound test of 14 September - forty-three doublings, and the only genuine compounds Colombian - SURVIVES THIS, and the Navarrete household is still the only Spanish instance. *** The test was right and this was the forty-fourth doubling.

column1: *** WHAT THE SWEEP DID TURN UP: A FORENAME ***
column2: the same 26, read for shape rather than for place
column3: *** THREE SPANISH-BORN PRUDENCIO LERENAS EMIGRATING, b. 1892, 1898 and 1899 ***
column4: Prudencio Lerena b.1899 of Najera to New Orleans 1931; Prudencio Lerena b.1892 to New Orleans 1939; Prudencio Velazoo [Velasco] Lerena b.1898 to Brownsville 1946. Alongside Restituto Lerena b.1904 (Boston 1921) and Felipe Mauricio Lerena b.1902 of Bilbao (San Francisco 1922).
column5: *** PRUDENCIO is the forename of one of the two Navarrete brothers - Prudencio Benito LERENA y LERENA. *** Three more of them leaving Spain in the next generation is a forename running in a family, and Najera is twenty kilometres from Navarrete. *** Index-level only: not one of these has been opened, and none is tiered. *** It is a direction, not a finding.

column1: *** AND A SPANISH LERENA HOUSEHOLD IN BUENOS AIRES IN 1895 ***
column2: the same 26 - Argentine National Census of 1895
column3: *** LEANDRO LERENA, b. 1857 in SPAIN, and EMILIA LERENA, b. 1886 in SPAIN, in one household ***
column4: Seccion 18, Subdivision 34, Ciudad de Buenos Aires. Both recorded as born in Spain, which is rare in this archive: almost every Argentine Lerena it has traced is Uruguayan-born.
column5: *** THE NAVARRETE BROTHERS WERE DEPENDIENTES IN BUENOS AIRES BY 1900, five years after this census, and this is a Spanish-born Lerena household already in the city. *** Not joined to them, and not opened - the census entry is the whole of it. *** Worth an hour before the Catastro, because it is reachable and the Catastro is a walk. ***
